title: Make architecture ratchet scanning syntactically sound and fail closed
description:
## Finding

The shared shrink-only architecture-ratchet scanner does not parse Rust conditional predicates. It strips only leading `not(` / `any(` / `all(` wrappers and then checks only the first predicate token. A target predicate later in a Boolean list is invisible.

This is not hypothetical drift: `thegn-host/src/profile.rs` contains several `#[cfg(all(feature = "profiling", unix))]` and `#[cfg(not(all(feature = "profiling", unix)))]` attributes outside `src/platform/`, while the host platform allowlist has no `profile.rs` entry and the 'new violation impossible' test passes.

The same utility also ignores `cfg_attr`, strips `//` without respecting Rust string literals, and silently omits directory entries/files on read or path errors. These fail-open behaviors make a green ratchet result weaker than the documented exhaustive source invariant.

## Evidence at 299fc13

* `crates/thegn-core/src/test_support/ratchet.rs:93-129` repeatedly removes wrappers but never walks comma-separated sibling predicates. For `all(feature = "profiling", unix)`, the first remaining token is `feature`, so `unix` is never examined.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/profile.rs:12,112,117,119` uses exactly this missed predicate ordering outside the designated `platform/` seam.
* `test/platform-cfg-host-ratchet.txt` has no `profile.rs`, proving the current test did not pin the file.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/platform_ratchet_tests.rs:10-23` promises that such conditionals are detected outside `platform/`.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/test_support/ratchet.rs:41-77` returns/filters entries on every traversal, metadata, path, or file-read failure instead of failing the test.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/test_support/ratchet.rs:80-90` treats the first `//` byte sequence as a comment even when it occurs in a Rust string literal.
* Identical copies of this implementation are compiled in `thegn-media` and `thegn-metrics`, so the false-negative behavior spans all five crate-level architecture ratchets.

## Impact

Cross-platform code can be introduced outside the intended platform seams while all architecture tests remain green.

## Required fix

* Parse or lex Rust attributes/comments soundly enough to inspect the complete `cfg` / `cfg_attr` predicate tree, independent of argument order and nesting.
* Make source-root traversal, directory-entry reads, path normalization, source reads, and allowlist reads fallible and fail the ratchet with the exact path/error.
* Preserve the leaf-crate dependency boundary: either provide a dependency-neutral sound implementation or centralize the scanner through an appropriate test-only boundary.
* Keep the core/media/metrics copies provably identical if duplication remains.
* Reconcile every newly exposed source file explicitly: move platform code to its seam or add a reasoned allowlist entry.
* Add adversarial tests for `all(feature, unix)`, nested predicates with platform terms in non-first positions, `cfg_attr`, comments, raw/ordinary strings containing `//`, and injected traversal/read failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Platform predicates are detected anywhere in a nested `cfg` or `cfg_attr` expression.
- [ ] The current `thegn-host/src/profile.rs` drift fails until explicitly reconciled.
- [ ] No filesystem/path/read error is converted into an omitted source or empty allowlist.
- [ ] Rust strings containing `//` cannot hide later code from a ratchet predicate.
- [ ] Core, service, host, media, and metrics ratchets exercise the repaired implementation.
- [ ] Regression tests demonstrate the former false negatives and fail-closed I/O behavior.
